### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ed33609731b0bc3b2da81c97242e9c8582d003d`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **167** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ed33609731b0bc3b2da81c97242e9c8582d003d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `14013912b9242a21ff32eda2498084c96887e410` — the merge of head `585e61981375b2d04780975e135e3dc6fba4d98f` into base `1ed33609731b0bc3b2da81c97242e9c8582d003d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 14013912b9242a21ff32eda2498084c96887e410 && git checkout 14013912b9242a21ff32eda2498084c96887e410
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1ed33609731b0bc3b2da81c97242e9c8582d003d 585e61981375b2d04780975e135e3dc6fba4d98f && git checkout -B drift-repro 1ed33609731b0bc3b2da81c97242e9c8582d003d && git merge --no-ff 585e61981375b2d04780975e135e3dc6fba4d98f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ed33609731b0bc3b2da81c97242e9c8582d003d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1ed33609731b0bc3b2da81c97242e9c8582d003d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

None pending.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the live tree:

1. `PUT /api/v1/meta/permission/:name` (draft and publish mode) now answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, nothing written, when an ACTIVE set of the name is held by a different owner. Placement is right: `protocol.ts:21007` sits after `refusePackagedBaseOverride` (`:20535`, so the packaged-lock `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` is not pre-empted), after the #23165 packageless-address rewrite (`:20599–20615`), and before the schema gate, the lock precondition (`:21670` `repo.put`) and every write. The store read propagates every non-benign failure (`rethrowUnlessMetadataStoreUnprovisioned`), so the predicate fails closed. **Right**, with the one exception judged in ④ must-fix 1.
2. `POST /api/v1/meta/permission/:name/publish` and `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/publish-drafts`: the promotion is judged on `promoteInto` before `repo.promoteDraft` (`:23081`); the batch tags the causal item and rolls back (`:24245–24300`), `failed[]` carries `code: RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. **Right.**
3. `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/duplicate` is a third face of the same door: `duplicatePackage` saves every copied set through `saveMetaItem(mode: 'publish', packageId: target)` under `renameName(row.name)` (`:25677–25680`, `:25768`), which swaps the source namespace prefix only when the name carries it. An unprefixed set name is now reported in `failed[]` with this refusal instead of being copied as a second holder. **Right behaviour, undeclared** — see ② and ④ should-fix 3.
4. `migrateStoredMetadata` re-saves stored rows through the same door ("records the refusal as the row's failure"): a deployment already holding one name under two owners now has both rows reported failed on `os migrate meta --stored`. **Right behaviour, undeclared.**
5. No public surface widens: `permissionSetNameCollisionRefusal` is not re-exported from `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`; the private method and the `SaveDoorRefusalHost` pick are internal. No error code is minted (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`/409 is ledgered). **Right.**
6. Holder reading: stored active environment rows by `package_id ?? null` (`storedOverlayEntries` never writes the `'sys_metadata'` sentinel — `withRowBinding` goes through `boundPackageOf`, which drops it), plus `registry.getItem(type, name)` counted only with a string `_packageId`. Boot hydration and the write-through register package-less rows with no `_packageId` (`protocol.ts:15454–15463`, `plugin.ts:3870`), so an environment-owned set is never mis-read as a package's. **Right.**
7. **Wrong:** the owner the save door hands the predicate is `saveWriteBinding`'s answer, which is the OWNER JUDGE's binding, not the write's address. For a draft save that names no package, `request.packageId` stays empty by design (`protocol.ts:20622–20633`, #23712) and the repository inherits the overlaid active row's package (#11087, `sys-metadata-repository.ts` `resolveWriteHead`); `saveWriteBinding` returns that inherited package only when the body carries a string `packageId`, else `null` (`protocol-save-door-refusals.ts:578–603`). A body with no `packageId` is legal ("absent: an absent key declares nothing", `permission-set-owner-binding.ts` verdict table). So the owning package's own draft edit through the console's plain `?mode=draft` save — the exact caller #11087 names — is judged owner `null` against holder `P` and refused as a foreign write, while the identical save in publish mode is accepted (the #23165 rewrite names `P`). The test's same-owner CONTROL passes `packageId: OWNER_B` explicitly and does not reach this path.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/harden-permission-set-name-cross-package.md`: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`, carrying `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker and a BREAKING before/now/owner/who-sees-it/remedy block. The PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line. `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green on the head, so the level stands as the gate's verdict (a REST accept-set narrowing that adds no protocol capability ships `patch`). `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: no authorable key, value or type changes; the `permission` entry keeps `supportsOverlay: true, allowEnvironmentOverlay: false, allowRuntimeCreate: true` (`metadata-plugin.zod.ts:1206`), which is the ADR-0005 premise the body cites. The "Who sees it" paragraph names the `PUT` and `publish-drafts` faces only; the duplicate face (①.3) and the stored-migration face (①.4) are consumers of the same door and are not named (④ should-fix 3) — a wording gap, not a level change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: an optional one-line note in `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` that a set name is unique across the deployment; not filed. Agreed not owed: the skill teaches grants by machine `name` and says nothing a cross-package name could rely on; `Metadata-protocol: none` means no new authorable capability to teach. ADR-0131 D4 already states "Studio refuses a name a managed package holds".
- `deviations`: PR body lacks the session-URL footer (durable attribution is in the commit trailers and the report comment); no assignee (no card); labels are the auto-labeller's. Seat matters, not contract matters; none escalated.
- Security path "detail withheld": the mechanism was read in the tree instead (①.1–①.7); nothing in the withheld measurement is needed for this verdict.
- Two derived families NOT MEASURED locally by the dev (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`): answered by `Build Core` and `Lint & Repo Gates` success on the head.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: ADR-0131 D4 (a grant names its set by bare name; the namespace is the environment registry's; Studio refuses a name a managed package holds), ADR-0086 D4 (a package never writes into a shared or foreign record), the maintainer rulings Q4 = A on #15196 ("positions, permission sets and capabilities each hold one namespace per deployment") and A on #22307 ("one name, one holder, on every path"). The registry already refuses the second holder at install and at cold boot (`SecurityCatalogNameConflictError`), and `security-catalog-namespace.ts` records that it deliberately does not judge "an environment-catalog save over a package-held name — that path keeps its own answers". This PR is that path's own answer, so it makes the spec's own refusal real at the metadata door and takes no declared capability away in principle: a cross-owner second set was never an authorable capability. Direction right; the implementation over-reaches at one consumer path and under-reaches at one door.

**Must-fix**

1. **The save door's owner is read from the wrong resolution, so the owning package's own draft edit is refused.** `protocol.ts:21007–21010` passes `writeBinding` (= `saveWriteBinding`, built for the ADR-0086 D3 owner judge: it reads the store only when the body carries a string `packageId`) as the write's owner. For a draft save naming no package over a package-bound active row with a body that omits `packageId`, the write lands in the inherited package `P` (#11087) while the predicate judges owner `null`, finds `P` foreign and answers `409 "this environment cannot save a second set of that name"`. The same body in publish mode is accepted (`:20615` names `P`). This contradicts the PR's own invariant ("the same-owner edit path is untouched") and the verdict table that legalises an absent `packageId`, and it refuses a path the door declares (#11087, the console's plain `?mode=draft` save). Fix: hand the predicate the binding the write lands in — the draft address's `into` (`draftAddress`, `:20626–20633`, already in scope; refuse-as-ambiguous when it is) for a draft save, `request.packageId` after the #23165 rewrite for a publish-mode save — and add a pin: owner `B` holds the active set, body without `packageId`, `mode: 'draft'`, no `packageId` on the request, expected `success: true`, draft bound to `B`.

**Should-fix**

2. **The restore door is not judged.** The sibling owner judge is asked at three doors — save, restore (`restoredBodyWriter` → `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses`, the save door's refusal family #25278 built for exactly this, "never a copy of a rule") and promotion — and `restoreVersion` writes an active row where none exists ("a missing active row yields null — the unbound row", then `put`). The new predicate is asked at two. Add it to `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses` against the binding the restore reads, with a pin through `rollbackMetaItem`, so the PR's "every door a body reaches active through" holds.
3. **Declare the faces.** The changeset's "Who sees it" should name `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/duplicate` (`failed[]` entry with these words for a set name without the source namespace prefix; the remedy "prefix it with your own module prefix" is the right one there) and the `os migrate meta --stored` re-save of pre-existing two-owner rows (both reported failed until one is renamed or deleted). Level unchanged.
4. **Envelope.** Rulings #15196 Q4 A and #22307 A fix this rule's envelope at `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` at install and at cold boot ("the same envelope, on every path"); the metadata door now answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` for the same condition, so a client reads two codes for one rule depending on the door. The body's defence (metadata-protocol's own unmanaged-install collisions answer 409) is a pre-existing split between the two packages, not a ruling. Either adopt `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`/422 here with the registry's words, or record in the predicate's docblock why this door keeps 409 and cite the ruling it departs from.
5. **A second reading of "who holds a name".** Ruling B on #22371 refused "a second reading of who holds a name beside the cold boot's, approximate on both sides, drifting over time", and the registry exports that reading (`findPackageHeldSecurityCatalogNames`). The predicate re-derives the package half from `getItem` (one item, no install claims, `securityCatalogClaims` unread) and the environment half from stored rows. Today the two agree wherever the install rule is in force; the drift risk is the one the ruling names. Either read the package half through the registry's export or state in the docblock why the door's reading must differ (it must count stored package-bound rows the cold boot does not see).
6. **#23165's residue.** The direct save used to mint a package-less row beside a package's row of the same name, and #23165 rules that "a package-less row beside the package's row is not a second package" for the write address. The predicate counts that residue as a second owner (`null` against `P`), so on such an item the owning package's publish-mode edit and the environment's edit are both refused, and the refusal's remedy ("edit the existing set in the package that owns it") is itself refused. Either exclude the package-less row beside a single package's row from the foreign set (the #23165 rule, applied to ownership), or word the refusal for that shape with the delete that clears it.

Test and ledger on the floor: the 10 cases pin both doors with paired controls; the engine double records `delete`/`findOne`/`update` in `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, matching the three asserts the file imports. The stub registry's `registerItem(type, item)` drops a third and fourth argument, which is harmless here (the write-through passes no `packageId` for the rows these cases write) but means the harness cannot see provenance the real registry stamps; the must-fix pin above needs no new double.
